requiredFindings.title: Correct the inherited entry-point state rule for FR-1 disclosures
requiredFindings.detail: The plan preserves the reference entryPoints.state rule, which returns none whenever all effect entry lists are empty, even with config-requires-evaluation. For example, vite.config.ts without index.html, next.config.js without routes, or an outside-subset pnpm carrier produces none. NE FR-1 and law item 16 require partial for a config needing evaluation. The wrapper cannot promise exactly four changes while inheriting this conflicting state rule.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Explicitly amend the reference state calculation for FR-1 disclosures, propagate it to product vectors, and add no-known-entry and mixed-recognizer cases. Keep any explicit override behavior separately specified.

requiredFindings.title: Enforce the entry-point ceiling across the unit
requiredFindings.detail: FR-4 sets maxEntryPointsPerUnit, but the proposed overflow policy examines one recognizer and drops only that recognizer when its own list exceeds 65536. A unit with 65536 Next.js route entries and a distinct Vite index.html exceeds the unit bound although neither result exceeds its individual schema maxItems.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Define the per-unit aggregate effective recognized-entry calculation and its bound, including overlap handling. Add 65536/65537 cases split across recognizers. An explicit all-or-nothing disclosure without truncation can be conservative, but it must apply at the owning unit scope and retain uncertainty.

requiredFindings.title: Do not equate explicit empty entryPoints with absence
requiredFindings.detail: The explicit override activates only for a nonempty resolved array. The configuration schema admits entryPoints: [], and the resolver preserves winning-leaf provenance. Law item 1 distinguishes absence (automatic) from an admitted higher-layer array replacing a lower array whole. A project/local explicit [] can clear a lower explicit list; the proposed check instead re-enables recognized defaults and permits recommendations as if configuration were absent.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Determine explicit intent from presence/winning provenance, define the effective empty-set result, and preserve higher-layer empty overrides. Add absent versus explicit-empty and lower-nonempty/higher-empty controls for recognition and recommendation generation.

requiredFindings.title: Keep the proposed YAML grammar a subset of scalar sequences
requiredFindings.detail: The stated plain-scalar exclusions reject colon-space only, so packages:\n  - foo:\n satisfies the proposed scalar rules although foo: is a block mapping entry, not a plain scalar. Colon followed by a tab has the same separator issue. The sequence-item production also needs explicit separation after the dash; -foo is scalar text rather than a block-sequence item.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Specify YAML-valid dash separation and plain-scalar colon termination/separation rules, then reject mapping-valued items and other non-scalar constructs with the existing disclosure. Add terminal-colon, colon-tab, dash-without-separation and quoted counterparts to the grammar vectors.

requiredFindings.title: Settle TOML parser resource differences before defining exact oracle equality
requiredFindings.location: PLAN-r1.md section 1, lines 46-51 and 68-73; section 3, line 133
requiredFindings.detail: The oracle uses tomllib while the product uses parse_toml, which has a 4 MiB byte cap, a recursion limit and a 1000000-node limit. A valid Cargo document with a usable package/workspace table plus a sufficiently large unrelated array can parse in tomllib and fail NodeLimit in the product. The current plan requires every oracle vector to reproduce byte for byte but supplies no resource-difference disposition or differential controls.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Declare how every parse_toml error maps to recognition disclosure and the shared Cargo-workspace fact. Align the oracle profile or label intentional product-bound divergences, following the existing B3-b parser-control precedent. Include usable tables plus unrelated deep/wide fields and exact/past-bound inputs.

requiredFindings.title: Map unit-relative recognition paths before proposing project settings
requiredFindings.detail: Recognition effects are unit-root-relative, while recommendations are placed in a project configuration carrier. For a unit rooted at apps/web, recognized src/main.ts must not be proposed as project discovery.entryPoints src/main.ts. That wrong path can pass the actual resolver because syntax admission does not establish unit ownership. Deferring all path joins to C4 leaves B2-d3 recommendation evidence incorrect.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Specify the unit-root-to-project path mapping for proposed entryPoints and ignore conventions, preserve unit identity through aggregation, and test nested units and colliding relative names. Keep this recommendation mapping separate from the still-unaccepted FR-6 change to retained recognition paths.
